  "textEditContent": "# Styling in DriftBoard\n\nDriftBoard's styling strategy is built on modern, utility-first principles to ensure consistency, maintainability, and rapid development. We use a combination of **Tailwind CSS** for utility classes and **ShadCN/UI** for base components.\n\n## 1. Tailwind CSS\n\n[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) is a utility-first CSS framework. Instead of writing custom CSS classes like &#96;.btn-primary&#96;, you compose styles directly in your HTML/JSX using pre-existing utility classes.\n\n**Example:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n// Instead of this:\n// &lt;button class=\"btn btn-primary\"&gt;Save&lt;/button&gt;\n// .btn { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; }\n// .btn-primary { background-color: blue; color: white; }\n\n// We do this:\n&lt;button className=\"py-2 px-4 bg-blue-500 text-white font-semibold rounded-lg shadow-md hover:bg-blue-700\"&gt;\n  Save\n&lt;/button&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Key Advantages:\n\n- **Speed**: You can build custom designs without ever leaving your HTML.\n- **Consistency**: You're using values from a predefined design system (spacing, colors, etc.), which keeps the UI consistent.\n- **Performance**: Tailwind automatically removes all unused CSS in production builds, resulting in a very small final CSS file.\n- **Responsive Design**: You can apply utilities for specific screen sizes using prefixes like &#96;md:&#96;, &#96;lg:&#96;, etc.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n&lt;div className=\"w-full md:w-1/2 lg:w-1/3\"&gt;\n  {/* This div is full-width on small screens, 50% on medium screens, and 33% on large screens */}\n&lt;/div&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 2. ShadCN/UI\n\n[ShadCN/UI](https://ui.shadcn.com/) is not a traditional component library. Instead, it's a collection of beautifully designed, reusable components that you copy and paste directly into your project.\n\n### Key Features:\n\n- **You Own the Code**: The components live in &#96;src/frontend/src/components/ui/&#96;. This means you can modify them to fit your exact needs without fighting against a library's opinions.\n- **Built on Radix UI**: The components are built on top of [Radix UI](https://www.radix-ui.com/), which provides accessible, unstyled, and highly functional primitives. This handles all the tricky parts like accessibility (ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation) and state management for things like dialogs and dropdowns.\n- **Styled with Tailwind CSS**: The components are styled using Tailwind CSS, so they fit perfectly into our existing styling system.\n\n### How We Use It:\n\nWe use ShadCN/UI components as the foundational building blocks for our application.\n\n- **Directory**: &#96;src/frontend/src/components/ui/&#96;\n- **Examples**: &#96;Button.tsx&#96;, &#96;Dialog.tsx&#96;, &#96;Input.tsx&#96;, &#96;Card.tsx&#96; (the primitive, not the Kanban card).\n\nWhen we need a more complex UI element, we compose these primitives together. For example, our &#96;BoardForm&#96; might use the ShadCN &#96;Dialog&#96;, &#96;Input&#96;, and &#96;Button&#96; components to create the form interface.\n\n## 3. Custom CSS and Theming\n\nWhile Tailwind covers most of our needs, we have a few global styles and CSS variables defined in &#96;src/frontend/src/index.css&#96;.\n\n- **CSS Variables**: We define our primary color palette as CSS variables in the &#96;:root&#96; selector. This allows for easy theming and consistency. Tailwind is configured to use these variables.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;css\n/* From index.css */\n:root {\n  --background: 0 0% 100%;\n  --foreground: 222.2 84% 4.9%;\n  --primary: 222.2 47.4% 11.2%;\n  /* ... and so on */\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis combination of Tailwind and ShadCN/UI gives us the best of both worlds: the speed and consistency of a utility-first framework, and the flexibility and ownership of custom-built components.\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/driftboard/docs/react/custom-hooks.md)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/driftboard/docs/react/custom-hooks.md)",
  "isConfirmed": true,
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "# Custom Hooks in DriftBoard\n\nIn React, a **custom hook** is a JavaScript function whose name starts with &#96;use&#96; and that can call other hooks. They are a powerful tool for reusing stateful logic between components without having to change your component hierarchy.\n\nIn DriftBoard, we use custom hooks to encapsulate and share logic that is used in multiple places, keeping our components cleaner and more focused on rendering the UI. Our custom hooks are located in &#96;src/frontend/src/hooks/&#96;.\n\n## Why Use Custom Hooks?\n\nImagine you have logic to detect the screen width to render different layouts for mobile and desktop. You might need this in several components. Instead of duplicating this logic everywhere, you can extract it into a custom hook.\n\n**Without a custom hook (Bad):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n// ComponentA.tsx\nconst [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth);\nuseEffect(() =&gt; {\n  const handleResize = () =&gt; setWidth(window.innerWidth);\n  window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);\n  return () =&gt; window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize);\n}, []);\nconst isMobile = width &lt; 768;\n\n// ComponentB.tsx\n// ... same exact logic duplicated here ...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**With a custom hook (Good):**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n// hooks/useViewport.ts\nexport const useViewport = () =&gt; {\n  const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth);\n  // ... effect logic ...\n  return { width, isMobile: width &lt; 768 };\n};\n\n// ComponentA.tsx\nconst { isMobile } = useViewport();\n\n// ComponentB.tsx\nconst { isMobile } = useViewport();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Custom Hooks in DriftBoard\n\nHere are some examples of custom hooks you might find or create in the DriftBoard project:\n\n### &#96;useBoards&#96;\n\nA potential hook to encapsulate the logic for fetching and managing the list of boards. It would wrap the RTK Query hook and could provide additional computed values.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useGetBoardsQuery } from '@/api/api';\n\nexport const useBoards = () =&gt; {\n  const { data: boards = [], isLoading, isError } = useGetBoardsQuery();\n\n  // We could add more logic here, e.g., sorting or filtering\n  const sortedBoards = [...boards].sort((a, b) =&gt; a.name.localeCompare(b.name));\n\n  return {\n    boards: sortedBoards,\n    isLoading,\n    isError,\n  };\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### &#96;useDebounce&#96;\n\nA common utility hook to debounce a value. This is useful for features like search, where you want to wait until the user has stopped typing before firing an API request.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useState, useEffect } from 'react';\n\nexport function useDebounce&lt;T&gt;(value: T, delay: number): T {\n  const [debouncedValue, setDebouncedValue] = useState&lt;T&gt;(value);\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    const handler = setTimeout(() =&gt; {\n      setDebouncedValue(value);\n    }, delay);\n\n    return () =&gt; {\n      clearTimeout(handler);\n    };\n  }, [value, delay]);\n\n  return debouncedValue;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### &#96;useAuth&#96;\n\nA simple hook to provide convenient access to the authentication state from the Redux store.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useSelector } from 'react-redux';\nimport { RootState } from '@/store';\n\nexport const useAuth = () =&gt; {\n  const authState = useSelector((state: RootState) =&gt; state.auth);\n  return {\n    ...authState,\n    isAuthenticated: !!authState.token,\n  };\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy creating and using custom hooks, we adhere to the **DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)** principle and make our stateful logic portable and easy to test in isolation.\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/driftboard/docs/react/drag-and-drop.md)",
  "isConfirmed": true,
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "# Drag and Drop in DriftBoard\n\nA core feature of any Kanban board is the ability to visually reorder items. In DriftBoard, this functionality is powered by **&#96;@dnd-kit&#96;**, a modern, lightweight, and highly performant library for drag and drop in React.\n\n## Why &#96;@dnd-kit&#96;?\n\nWe chose &#96;@dnd-kit&#96; for several key reasons:\n\n- **Accessibility**: It's built with accessibility in mind, providing features like keyboard support and screen reader announcements out of the box.\n- **Performance**: It's designed to be fast and avoids common performance pitfalls associated with drag-and-drop libraries.\n- **Customizability**: It's a \"headless\" library, meaning it provides the core logic but gives us full control over the rendering and styling of our components.\n- **Touch Support**: It works seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices.\n\n## Core Concepts of &#96;@dnd-kit&#96;\n\nThe implementation in DriftBoard revolves around a few key concepts from the library.\n\n### 1. &#96;DndContext&#96;\n\nThis is the main provider component that wraps the part of your application where you want to enable drag and drop. It provides the context for all sensors, collision detection algorithms, and event listeners. In DriftBoard, this is typically placed at the top level of the &#96;BoardDetailPage&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n&lt;DndContext onDragEnd={handleDragEnd}&gt;\n  {/* All your draggable lists and cards go here */}\n&lt;/DndContext&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Sensors\n\nSensors are how &#96;@dnd-kit&#96; detects input from different devices. We use:\n- **&#96;PointerSensor&#96;**: For mouse, touch, and stylus input.\n- **&#96;KeyboardSensor&#96;**: For enabling keyboard-based reordering for accessibility.\n\n### 3. &#96;SortableContext&#96;\n\nTo create a list of items that can be reordered, we wrap them in a &#96;SortableContext&#96;. This context needs an array of the unique IDs of the sortable items and a sorting strategy.\n\n- **Lists**: The columns on our board are wrapped in a horizontal &#96;SortableContext&#96;.\n- **Cards**: The cards within each list are wrapped in a vertical &#96;SortableContext&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n// For a list of cards\n&lt;SortableContext items={cardIds} strategy={verticalListSortingStrategy}&gt;\n  {cards.map(card =&gt; &lt;SortableCard key={card.id} id={card.id} /&gt;)}\n&lt;/SortableContext&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 4. &#96;useSortable&#96; Hook\n\nThis hook is used inside a component to make it draggable, droppable, and sortable within a &#96;SortableContext&#96;. It provides the necessary props and event listeners that you need to attach to your component's DOM node.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useSortable } from '@dnd-kit/sortable';\nimport { CSS } from '@dnd-kit/utilities';\n\nconst SortableCard = ({ id }) =&gt; {\n  const {\n    attributes,\n    listeners,\n    setNodeRef,\n    transform,\n    transition,\n  } = useSortable({ id });\n\n  const style = {\n    transform: CSS.Transform.toString(transform),\n    transition,\n  };\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div ref={setNodeRef} style={style} {...attributes} {...listeners}&gt;\n      {/* Card content */}\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 5. Event Handling (&#96;onDragEnd&#96;)\n\nThe &#96;onDragEnd&#96; event handler is the most critical piece of logic. It fires after a drag operation is completed. Inside this function, we:\n\n1.  **Check if a move occurred**: We compare the &#96;active&#96; (the item being dragged) and &#96;over&#96; (the droppable area it landed on) properties of the event object.\n2.  **Determine the type of move**: Was a card moved within the same list, or to a different list? Was a list reordered?\n3.  **Dispatch an action**: We call a mutation from our RTK Query API to update the item's position on the backend.\n4.  **Use Optimistic Updates**: To make the UI feel instantaneous, we update the local Redux state immediately, assuming the API call will succeed. RTK Query handles rolling back the change automatically if the API call fails.\n",

}
